description: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled brings the authentic, smoky flavors of India to your home, featuring succulent chicken marinated in a rich, spicy yogurt blend. The intense heat of charcoal imparts a distinct char and deep flavor that is simply irresistible. This classic dish promises a delightful culinary experience, perfect for any special dinner or gathering.

ingredients.notes: skin removed, bone-in preferred, deeply scored

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the chicken pieces and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make deep, diagonal slits (2-3 per piece) on the chicken to ensure the marinade penetrates deeply and cooks evenly.

instructions.title: First Marinade Application
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the prepared chicken with salt and fresh lemon juice. Rub these ingredients all over the chicken pieces, ensuring they are well coated. Let the chicken rest in this first marinade for 10-15 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together the hung yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala powder, Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and mustard oil. If desired, add the red food color for that classic tandoori hue.

instructions.title: Combine and Marinate
instructions.text: Add the chicken from the first marinade into the bowl with the second yogurt-spice mixture. Using your hands, thoroughly coat each chicken piece, ensuring the marinade gets into all the slits. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for maximum flavor absorption.

instructions.title: Preheat the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create both a direct high-heat zone and an indirect medium-heat zone. Let the coals heat until they are glowing red and covered with a light grey ash.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto skewers, ensuring they are not overcrowded. Place the skewers over the direct heat zone of the grill. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently, until they develop a nice char and the marinade sticks well.

instructions.title: Finish Cooking and Baste
instructions.text: Move the partially cooked chicken to the indirect heat zone. Continue grilling, turning occasionally, and basting with any leftover marinade or a little oil, for another 10-15 minutes. Cook until the chicken is tender, cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F or 74°C), and beautifully charred.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Carefully remove the grilled tandoori chicken from the skewers. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro, and serve hot with fresh lemon wedges, onion rings, and a side of mint chutney or warm naan bread.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, use hung yogurt (drain excess water from plain yogurt) for a thicker, richer marinade that clings better to the chicken.
The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will become. Overnight marination is highly recommended.
Ensure your charcoal grill is properly preheated and you have both direct and indirect heat zones to perfectly char the chicken without burning it and then cook it through.
article:
Tandoori Chicken is a global culinary icon, celebrated for its vibrant color, smoky aroma, and succulent texture. While traditionally cooked in a scorching hot clay tandoor oven, mastering this dish at home is entirely possible and incredibly rewarding, especially when you embrace the power of charcoal grilling. This method not only replicates the authentic smoky char but also makes it a fantastic addition to your repertoire of Indian dinner recipes. Get ready to embark on a flavorful journey to create an unforgettable Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled experience right in your backyard.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

At its heart, Tandoori Chicken is chicken marinated in a mixture of yogurt and a myriad of spices, then traditionally cooked at high heat. The "tandoor" is a cylindrical clay oven, known for its intense heat and ability to impart a distinctive smoky flavor and beautiful char. When we talk about Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, we're essentially recreating that tandoor magic using a charcoal grill. The intense, direct heat from the charcoal mimics the tandoor's searing temperatures, while the burning charcoal itself infuses the chicken with an irresistible smoky depth that a gas grill simply can't match.

The marinade is key. It typically includes thick plain yogurt, which tenderizes the chicken and acts as a base for the spices. Ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and a blend of ground spices like Kashmiri red chili powder (for its vibrant color and mild heat), turmeric, cumin, coriander, and garam masala create the signature flavor profile. The result is tender, juicy chicken with beautifully charred edges and a complex, aromatic taste – a true showstopper among Indian dinner recipes. The unique flavor of Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken comes from this combination of a rich marinade and the smoky kiss of the grill.

## Ingredients You Need

Preparing an authentic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken requires fresh ingredients and a well-balanced spice blend. Here's what you'll need:

For the Chicken:
*   1 whole chicken, about 3-4 lbs, cut into 8-10 pieces (or 6-8 chicken thighs/drumsticks)
*   2 tbsp lemon juice (for first marinade)
*   1 tsp salt (for first marinade)

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup thick plain yogurt (Greek yogurt works well; if using regular yogurt, drain excess water)
*   2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder (for color and mild heat, adjust to preference)
*   1 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp cumin powder
*   1 tsp coriander powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp black pepper powder
*   1/2 tsp fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed (optional, but highly recommended for authentic flavor)
*   1-2 tbsp lemon juice
*   1 tsp salt (adjust to taste)
*   Red or orange food color (optional, for vibrant restaurant-style color)

For Grilling:
*   Oil or melted butter for basting

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Now, let's get to grilling your perfect Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken. Follow these steps for a delicious outcome:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Rinse the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make deep gashes (2-3 per piece) into the thickest parts of the chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor.
2.  **First Marinade (Optional but Recommended):** In a large bowl, toss the chicken pieces with 2 tablespoons of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub it in well. Let it sit for 15-20 minutes. This step helps tenderize the chicken and enhances flavor absorption.
3.  **Prepare the Main Marinade:** In a separate large bowl, combine the thick yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper powder, crushed kasoori methi (if using), 1-2 tablespoons of lemon juice, and 1 teaspoon of salt. If using food color, add a few drops and mix until you achieve a vibrant orange-red hue. Mix everything thoroughly until well combined.
4.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the chicken pieces (from the first marinade, no need to rinse) to the main marinade. Ensure every piece is generously coated. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness.
5.  **Prepare the Grill:** Light your charcoal about 30-45 minutes before you plan to cook. Arrange the charcoal for direct medium-high heat. You're looking for coals that are glowing orange with a light layer of ash. Clean your grill grates and lightly oil them to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grill the Chicken:** Once the grill is ready, place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals. Leave some space between pieces to ensure even cooking.
7.  **Cook and Turn:** Grill for about 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently to prevent burning and ensure even cooking. As the chicken cooks, it will develop beautiful char marks. Baste the chicken periodically with oil or melted butter during the last 10-15 minutes of cooking. This adds moisture and a rich flavor.
8.  **Check for Doneness:** Continue grilling until the chicken is cooked through, with an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) at its thickest part. The total grilling time will vary depending on the size of your chicken pieces and the heat of your grill, typically ranging from 25-40 minutes.
9.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in more tender and flavorful chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that restaurant-quality Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken at home is all about attention to detail.

*   **Thick Yogurt is Key:** Using thick plain yogurt or Greek yogurt prevents the marinade from dripping off the chicken. If your yogurt is thin, strain it through a cheesecloth for an hour or two.
*   **Don't Skip the Slashes:** Deep gashes are crucial for the marinade to penetrate, ensuring the chicken is flavorful to the bone.
*   **Long Marination:** This is perhaps the most important tip. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Control Your Heat:** A medium-high direct heat is what you want. If the heat is too high, the outside will burn before the inside cooks. If it's too low, the chicken will dry out. Use a two-zone fire if possible, with a cooler zone for moving chicken if it's charring too quickly.
*   **Baste Generously:** Basting with oil or melted butter keeps the chicken moist and helps achieve that beautiful golden-brown crust.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of grilling it.
*   **Use a Meat Thermometer:** This is the safest way to ensure your chicken is perfectly cooked and juicy, not undercooked or dry.
*   **Add Wood Chips:** For an even deeper smoky flavor, throw a handful of pre-soaked wood chips (hickory or applewood work well) directly onto the hot coals during grilling.

## Serving Suggestions

Once your succulent Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is ready, it's time to assemble an authentic Indian dinner.

*   **Bread:** Serve it piping hot with fresh naan bread, roti, or paratha to scoop up the flavorful juices.
*   **Chutney:** A refreshing mint-coriander chutney is the perfect accompaniment, offering a cool contrast to the smoky chicken.
*   **Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumbers, tomatoes, and onions with a lemon dressing) adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Onion Rings and Lemon Wedges:** Garnish with thinly sliced red onion rings and plenty of lemon wedges for squeezing over the chicken just before eating.
*   **Rice:** For a more complete meal, pair it with fluffy basmati rice or aromatic Jeera Rice (cumin rice).
*   **Drinks:** A cooling glass of Lassi (yogurt drink) complements the meal beautifully.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is unbeatable, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit different tastes and preferences.

*   **Chicken Parts:** Feel free to use boneless chicken thighs or breast pieces for quicker cooking. Just adjust grilling time accordingly (boneless breasts might dry out easily, so keep an eye on them). Chicken drumsticks are also a popular choice.
*   **Vegetarian Alternatives:** The Tandoori marinade is incredibly versatile! You can use it for paneer tikka (Indian cheese), mushroom tikka, or a mix of vegetables like bell peppers, onions, and zucchini, grilled on skewers.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder and add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a finely chopped green chili for extra heat if you prefer a spicier dish.
*   **Flavor Enhancers:** A touch of mustard oil in the marinade can add a pungent, authentic kick. A little honey or brown sugar can balance the spices and aid in caramelization.
*   **Alternative Cooking Methods:** If charcoal grilling isn't an option, you can use a gas grill (you'll miss some of the smoke, but it will still be delicious), bake it in an oven on a high heat setting (broiler for char), or even use an air fryer for smaller pieces. However, for that true smoky essence, Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is the way to go.

Bringing the flavors of a traditional Indian tandoor oven to your home grill is an incredibly satisfying culinary adventure. With this comprehensive guide, you're well-equipped to create a Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled that will impress your family and friends, making it a cherished addition to your collection of favorite Indian dinner recipes. Enjoy the vibrant colors, intoxicating aromas, and succulent taste of this timeless classic!
